terms.definition: A table of predicted and actual class counts. In binary classification, its four entries are true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives. It is tied to a chosen positive class and, for probability-based classifiers, to the threshold used to turn scores into labels.

The share of predicted positive cases that are actually positive, calculated as $TP/(TP+FP)$. It is useful when false positive alerts are costly, but is undefined if the classifier predicts no positives.

The share of actual positive cases correctly predicted positive, calculated as $TP/(TP+FN)$. It is also called sensitivity or true positive rate, and is undefined when there are no actual positive cases.

The share of actual negative cases incorrectly predicted positive, calculated as $FP/(FP+TN)$. It is plotted on the horizontal axis of a conventional ROC curve. It is not specificity, which is $TN/(TN+FP)$.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall, $2PR/(P+R)$. It combines these two measures into one score but does not include true negatives directly or encode an application’s error costs.

A cutoff applied to a model score or estimated probability to produce a classification decision. Changing the threshold changes predicted labels and therefore can change confusion-matrix counts and derived metrics.

The difference between a regression prediction and its observed value, here defined as $r_i=\hat{y}_i-y_i$. Under this sign convention, positive residuals indicate overprediction and negative residuals indicate underprediction.

The average magnitude of regression residuals, $\frac{1}{n}\sum_i|r_i|$. It remains in the target variable’s units and does not cancel positive and negative errors, though its average can still be affected by large errors.

The number of linearly independent rows or columns of a matrix. Rank reveals algebraic dependencies, such as redundant columns in a design matrix, but does not measure predictive performance or numerical conditioning.

A column containing a leading nonzero entry selected during elimination. Pivot columns identify independent columns under the elimination procedure. In `matrix-audit`, their indices are reported starting at zero.

A scalar associated with a square matrix that is zero exactly when the matrix is singular. It is not defined by this utility for rectangular matrices, and a nonzero determinant alone does not guarantee a well-conditioned numerical problem.
